admission_apply.text: You turn the rule. NEAR meets the thumb; the inches decline that courtesy.

native.admission_inspect: A dry bone rule, thumb-long. FAR is inked at the near end, and the ink looks wet.
apply_texts: A stopped tick in the bone arrives before the turn, then pretends it did not.
It will not turn again. Both ends keep their claims, each a little too exact.
The warmth shifts before the bone does, and the ink stays perfectly calm.
Turned back, FAR is restored. The exactness has simply changed its loyalty.
You reverse the rule. It becomes exact, which makes the near end less true.
You turn it back. FAR returns, yet the warmth remains with the end just lost.
You turn the rule. NEAR meets the thumb; the inches decline that courtesy.
inspect_texts: A dry bone rule, thumb-long. FAR is inked at the near end, and the ink looks wet.
A hairline like an undecided latch crosses the second inch. Both ends say FIRST.
Both ends read FIRST. The length is the same, and the sameness does not help.
FAR is back under the thumb, but FIRST remains on the end now called far.
NEAR has come under the thumb. The inches, unasked, still leave from there.
NEAR is correct, and the warmth disagrees, arriving from the end called FAR.
Reversed, the rule is consistent. It is consistent about the wrong premise.
The marks agree together and disagree with the hand. The mismatch is exact.
Warm bone, cold ink. The end not held seems to have been counted already.
native.name: The Far-Near Rule
